messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: oncall-sre. High tail latency detected for customer 'Lyra' (single-tenant). p99 streaming latency > 18s, p95 ~ 1.8s. svc: inference-host-lyra-dedicated-1
oncall-sre: I'm on it. Opening a triage channel here. Can someone from eng-runtime join? :raising_hand:
eng-runtime: I'm here. seeing a big skew on streaming tail tokens. p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 1.7s, but p99 jumps to 18-22s for some sessions.
eng-platform: Any recent deploys to Lyra tenant?
eng-runtime: No deploys in the last 6 hours. Resource metrics look OK: GPU utilisation ~ 60%, but CPU for sidecars is spiking and there are many concurrent long-lived streaming sessions.
customer-success: Lyra reports users seeing long stalls; they called support. Lyra contact is @lyra-sre.
lyra-sre: We're seeing a job that fanouts ~600 concurrent streaming requests every 5 minutes — an ETL-style summary job. It wasn't throttled. We can add client-side backoff but need help server-side.
support: We told Lyra to pause their scheduled job temporarily. They've paused it for now.
oncall-sre: Good. Immediate mitigation options: 1) Route some traffic to a fallback lower-capacity model variant; 2) Temporarily increase dedicated pool headroom; 3) Apply token-level rate limiting for Lyra; 4) Enable aggressive prefix KV caching if possible. Thoughts?
eng-runtime: Quick wins: enable prefix (KV) caching for Lyra's model profile and raise max-concurrent-sessions on that pool by +25% (hotfix autoscale). Also flip streaming stall detection to aggressive re-emit heuristics to avoid long waiting loops. I can push a config change in 2-3m.
eng-platform: I'll bump the dedicated pool (lyra-dedicated-1) from 8->10 GPUs to get immediate throughput. Will trigger capacity scale in 30s.
prod: Any customer-visible change we should message?
customer-success: Tell Lyra we suspect scheduled storm and we've paused their job; we'll increase capacity and apply caching. We'll ask them not to re-enable until we confirm.
eng-runtime: Pushing prefix cache: added cache_profile: lyra-bulk-prefix with TTL 30m and max_entries 20k. Command: ```rcctl set cache-profile lyra-bulk-prefix --ttl=1800 --max=20000 --apply-to=lyra-model-v2```
incident-bot: Deploy job queued: deploy/eng-runtime/cache-profile/3170000001 (CI link: https://ci.redwood/3170000001)
ops: Noted the pool scale. Watching for p99.
eng-runtime: Live logs show repeated stalls where a streaming connection pauses ~15-20s then resumes. Sample log: ```[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] conn_id=abc123 session=streaming prompt_len=1200 kv_hits=0 stall=18.4s downstream_write=0.0s```
eng-platform: Pool scale done. Added 2 GPUs to lyra-dedicated-1, nodes came up in ~45s.
oncall-sre: p99 decreased from 18-22s to ~9s after pool scale and cache flip. Still above SLO (p99 target 1.5s).
eng-runtime: Flipped aggressive streaming stall bailout: now if stdout has no progress for 3s we re-evaluate and either fallback or restart stream with a resume token. This reduced the long tails on a subset of sessions.
lyra-sre: After our pause, we re-ran parts of the job with slower fanout and the p99 is back down to ~3s. There's a problematic prompt pattern that triggers large KV cache churn: many sessions start with long shared prefix then append unique suffixes, invalidating prefix reuse.
devex: Can we recommend to Lyra a structural change? Suggest they pipeline large fanouts to batch generation (single request with multiple items) or use embeddings for pre-summarization.
product: We should capture this as a runbook: 'single-tenant scheduled fanout storm' — include autoscale thresholds, prefix caching whitelists, client rate-limits.
eng-runtime: Agreed. I'll open a post-incident PR with step-by-step mitigation and a config flag to auto-detect scheduled-fanout patterns (high concurrent streams with similar prefix hash).
oncall-sre: Handoff: oncall-sre -> eng-runtime for root cause and permanent mitigations. oncall-sre remains monitoring until 3170000850.
eng-runtime: For RCA: hypothesis is combination of (1) synchronous scheduled fanout creating high concurrency; (2) long identical prompt prefixes with unique suffixes causing KV cache thrash and preventing effective prefix reuse; (3) streaming stall behavior that kept connections open while backend did heavy work for some sessions. We'll validate and surface telemetry.
lyra-sre: We'll iterate on our client-side backoff and batching, but appreciate the help. Please share any specific prompt patterns we should avoid.
eng-runtime: We'll export a small sample (anonymized) of prefix hashes and request patterns; send via secure support ticket.
support: Logged ticket TKT-2026-451 for sharing telemetry and contact sync.
oncall-sre: Closing incident thread for active mitigation; if p99 stays under 3s for 20m we'll do formal postmortem. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
eng-platform: FYI alert rule update suggested: if single-tenant traffic spike > 200 concurrent streaming sessions AND kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.2 -> auto-scale + apply cache_profile. Opening infra issue.
eng-runtime: I'll follow up with a detailed remediation PR and recommended guardrails for Dedicated tenants.
product: Adding to backlog: improve per-tenant hard limits and scheduled-job detection UI in the Console.
incident-bot: Incident resolved (soft) at 3170000850.
